To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the invariant cross sections of the target fragmentation domain are determined by the source parameters which are independent of the projectile-target combination and of the collision energy.

at high enough energies the proton source in a nucleus-nucleus interaction can be described as a universal, highly heated object with a velocity that depends on the collision conditions and with a nucleon content that increases with the projectile-target mass ratio.

the universal source is a highly excited system, the excitation energy being about 100 MeV/nucleus, and that the source velocity and number of nucleons are functions of the projectile-target combination and collision energy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the properties of a highly excited nuclear source formed in the interaction of nuclei.
the problem of a universal source of nucleons in high energy nucleus collisions.
the search for universal characteristics of nucleus-nucleus interaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the source of protons in the target nucleus domain is an expanding hot nucleus, which is formed in high energy collisions and whose properties depend on the initial conditions of the interaction.

in the fragmentation region the interaction of nuclei at high energy leads to the formation of a universal source, the properties of which are determined by the initial energy of the colliding nuclei and by their masses.
the universal moving source is a real physical object and the proton spectra measured in high energy nucleus–nucleus collisions can be interpreted in terms of its properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the nucleus-nucleus collision process is described by a universal function which is determined by the excitation energy and the temperature of the source, the number of nucleon participants in the interaction and their average velocity.
the nucleus-nucleus collision is accompanied by the production of a highly heated, moving source of nucleons.

the nucleus-nucleus collision at high energies is a highly non-adiabatic process, which is accompanied by a strong heating of the system, but the excitation energy is not converted into the internal energy of the fragments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the universal source is a very compact object (the radius being ⪡ 1 fm), which means that the interaction of the projectile with the target nucleus is a local process.
the proton source is universal in the sense that it is independent of the projectile and target nuclei.
the source is a universal object, which can be considered as a new state of nuclear matter.
